goal: Create a new Python project with uv, add one third-party package, and run a script that imports it
success: In a brand-new project, uv run example.py imports a package added with uv add, prints its output, and exits 0

error_checks.note: Correct and complete, but the answer is the last 6 of about 50 lines; a newcomer sees a wall of version ranges first. The hint says to raise requires-python to >=3.11. Doing only that gives a second error, because .python-version still says 3.9. That second error is good (it names uv python pin), so recovery takes two rounds instead of one. The --frozen hint invites skipping the lock, which is the wrong move for a newcomer.
error_checks.better:
error: numpy>=2.1 needs Python 3.10 or newer, but this project allows Python 3.9 (requires-python = ">=3.9", .python-version = 3.9).
fix:   uv python pin 3.11 && set requires-python = ">=3.11" in pyproject.toml, then run uv add "numpy>=2.1" again
       (or pick an older version: uv add "numpy<2.1")
run with --verbose to see the full resolution.
